## Vardenafil (Levitra): Market Withdrawal, Black Box Warning, and Discontinuation

---

### 1. 🚫 Was It Withdrawn from the Market for Safety Reasons? **No.**


The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has determined that Levitra (vardenafil hydrochloride) oral tablets, 5 mg, 10 mg, and 20 mg, **were not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness**.



In a letter dated March 22, 2018, Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals, Inc. notified the FDA that Levitra (vardenafil hydrochloride) tablets were being discontinued, and the FDA moved the drug product to the "Discontinued Drug Product List" section of the Orange Book.



Bayer Pharmaceuticals had already told the FDA that they discontinued their ED medication for business reasons. The drug manufacturer said it had nothing to do with its safety or effectiveness — on three separate occasions.



The FDA carefully reviewed its files for records concerning the withdrawal of Levitra, and independently evaluated relevant literature and data for possible postmarketing adverse events. It reviewed the available evidence and determined that these drug products were **not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness**.


📌 **Source:** Federal Register, May 3, 2023 — [https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/03/2023-09365/determination-that-levitra-vardenafil-hydrochloride-oral-tablets-5-milligrams-10-milligrams-and-20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/03/2023-09365/determination-that-levitra-vardenafil-hydrochloride-oral-tablets-5-milligrams-10-milligrams-and-20)

### 2. ⚠️ Has Vardenafil Ever Received a Black Box Warning? **Petitioned, but not granted.**


On October 20, 2005, Public Citizen filed a petition with the FDA to add **black box warnings** to the professional product labels for the erectile dysfunction drugs sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra). The warnings were intended to alert prescribers to the possibility of **irreversible vision loss** with the use of these drugs.



There is mention of NAION (non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy) in the Precautions and Adverse Reactions sections of the professional labels for Viagra, Cialis, and Levitra. However, Public Citizen argued that FDA should immediately require a **black box warning** for NAION for the entire PDE5 inhibitor drug class — since, at the time, there were only "two inconspicuous paragraphs" in the label with no bolding or prominent titles to call attention to this serious adverse event.


The FDA did **not** grant the petition for a black box warning. Instead, warnings about NAION and sudden vision loss were added to the **Warnings and Precautions** section of the label (not as a black box). 
Physicians are advised to instruct patients to stop use of all PDE5 inhibitors, including vardenafil, and seek medical attention in the event of sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes, which could be a sign of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a rare cause of decreased vision, including permanent loss of vision, that has been reported rarely postmarketing.


📌 **Source (Public Citizen petition):** [https://www.citizen.org/article/petition-to-require-a-black-box-warning-for-erectile-dysfunction-drugs-sildenafil-viagra-tadalafil-cialis-and-vardenafil-levitra/](https://www.citizen.org/article/petition-to-require-a-black-box-warning-for-erectile-dysfunction-drugs-sildenafil-viagra-tadalafil-cialis-and-vardenafil-levitra/)

### 3. 🔴 Was It Discontinued for Safety Reasons? **No — it was a business decision.**


Levitra was discontinued in several markets for **business and commercial reasons**, not safety concerns. With patent expiration and strong competition from other ED medications and generics, maintaining the brand was no longer economically viable.



Importantly, the active ingredient (vardenafil) was not discontinued. Generic vardenafil remains fully available and FDA-, EMA-, and internationally approved. The safety profile of the drug has not changed, and clinical evidence supporting its effectiveness remains robust.



Previously, brand versions of vardenafil were available, but they have been discontinued. These brands were Levitra and Staxyn. Vardenafil is now only available as a generic medication.

Below I treat **PDE5A** as the relevant target and infer **vardenafil’s direction on PDE5A = inhibition** from its ChEMBL IC50/Ki activity, as you requested. ChEMBL-linked activity summaries and other pharmacology sources show vardenafil inhibits recombinant human **PDE5A** at low-nanomolar potency. ([guidetopharmacology.org](https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/GRAC/LigandActivityRangeVisForward?ligandId=7320&utm_source=openai))

## 1) Disease mechanism in idiopathic PAH, and whether PDE5A is deficient or overactive

**Core pathophysiological defect:** Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) is driven by **progressive remodeling and constriction of the pulmonary arteriolar bed**, causing **increased pulmonary vascular resistance** and elevated pulmonary arterial pressure. At the molecular level, one of the canonical disturbed pathways is the **nitric oxide (NO)–soluble guanylate cyclase–cGMP axis**, with **reduced NO signaling / reduced cGMP bioavailability**, alongside excess vasoconstrictor and proliferative signaling. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2664591/?utm_source=openai))

For **PDE5A specifically**, the literature supports that it is **increased/overactive in PAH rather than deficient**. Reviews of pulmonary vascular disease report that **PDE5 expression is greater in lung tissue from patients with pulmonary hypertension than in controls**, including diseased pulmonary vascular smooth muscle and remodeled distal vessels. Because PDE5A hydrolyzes cGMP, this higher PDE5A activity would further **lower cGMP signaling** in the pulmonary vasculature. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4352681/?utm_source=openai))

**Answer to (1):** For IPAH, **PDE5A is best classified as OVERACTIVE / upregulated**, not deficient. The primary molecular logic is: **reduced NO–cGMP signaling + increased PDE5A-mediated cGMP breakdown in diseased pulmonary vessels**. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4352681/?utm_source=openai))

## 2) Would vardenafil’s direct action on PDE5A correct or worsen that defect?

Given your constraint to focus **only on the direct action on PDE5A itself**:

- **Disease-side defect:** PDE5A is **overactive/upregulated** in IPAH. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4352681/?utm_source=openai))
- **Drug-side action on PDE5A:** vardenafil shows **inhibitory** activity against PDE5A in biochemical assays. ([guidetopharmacology.org](https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/GRAC/LigandActivityRangeVisForward?ligandId=7320&utm_source=openai))

Therefore, **vardenafil’s direct action on PDE5A would correct/compensate for the disease defect**, not worsen it, because it acts in the **opposite direction** to the abnormality (it inhibits an overactive cGMP-degrading enzyme). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4352681/?utm_source=openai))

## 3) Clinical-use anchor: is vardenafil or a close class analog used for IPAH or PDE5A-related disease?

**Yes — the class is clinically validated for PAH through PDE5A inhibition.**  
Although **vardenafil itself is not an approved PAH drug**, closely related **PDE5 inhibitors sildenafil and tadalafil** are established therapies for **WHO group 1 PAH**, including idiopathic PAH. CHEST guidance recommends an approved **PDE5 inhibitor** as one monotherapy option in appropriate treatment-naive PAH patients, and more recent treatment algorithms continue to recommend **ERA + PDE5 inhibitor** combinations for many patients. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4137591/?utm_source=openai))

More specifically:

- Reviews note that **sildenafil and tadalafil are the FDA-approved PDE5 inhibitors for PAH**, whereas **vardenafil has not been approved for PAH** and evidence for it is limited. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4636095/?utm_source=openai))
- The confirmed mechanism is **PDE5A inhibition**, which **reduces cGMP degradation**, thereby restoring/increasing **cGMP signaling** in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4636095/?utm_source=openai))

So the class anchor is strong: **PDE5A inhibition is a validated therapeutic mechanism in IPAH/PAH**, but the approved members are **sildenafil** and **tadalafil**, not vardenafil. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4137591/?utm_source=openai))

## Bottom line

1. **IPAH defect:** pulmonary vascular remodeling/constriction with impaired **NO–cGMP** signaling; **PDE5A is overactive/upregulated**, not deficient. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4352681/?utm_source=openai))  
2. **Vardenafil on PDE5A:** as a **PDE5A inhibitor**, it would **correct/compensate for** that target-level defect. ([guidetopharmacology.org](https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/GRAC/LigandActivityRangeVisForward?ligandId=7320&utm_source=openai))  
3. **Clinical anchor:** **Yes, the mechanism is clinically validated** for PAH via the same target class; **sildenafil and tadalafil** are approved/standard PDE5 inhibitors for PAH, while **vardenafil is not approved for PAH** but is a close in-class analog. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4137591/?utm_source=openai))

the FDA also determined that Levitra (vardenafil hydrochloride) tablets, 2.5 mg, were not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness.

the drug manufacturer said it had nothing to do with its safety or effectiveness on three occasions.



The Agency continues to list Levitra (vardenafil hydrochloride) oral tablets, 5 mg, 10 mg, and 20 mg, in the "Discontinued Drug Product List" section of the Orange Book. The "Discontinued Drug Product List" delineates, among other items, drug products that have been discontinued from marketing for reasons **other than** safety or effectiveness.

---

### 2. 🟡 Has Vardenafil Hydrochloride Received a Black Box Warning?

This is a nuanced point. The **FDA has not issued a traditional black box warning** on the Levitra/vardenafil label, but there have been significant label safety updates and calls for black box warnings:

- **Public Citizen Petition (2005):** 
In order to inform patients, the FDA was petitioned to require mandatory distribution of Medication Guides and to require manufacturers to establish a registry of patients diagnosed with NAION (Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy) — a condition triggered by blockage of blood flow to the eye, which is sudden, painless in onset, and frequently leads to permanent blindness.
 This petition requested a **black box warning** be added to the labels of Levitra, Viagra, and Cialis.
  - Source: https://www.citizen.org/article/petition-to-require-a-black-box-warning-for-erectile-dysfunction-drugs-sildenafil-viagra-tadalafil-cialis-and-vardenafil-levitra/

- **Hearing Loss Label Update:** 
The FDA announced that the manufacturers of Cialis, Levitra, and Viagra must change their labeling. The FDA instructed the drugmakers to display information on their drugs' potential risk of sudden hearing loss more prominently and to guide consumers on what to do if they experienced sudden problems with their hearing. The labeling changes resulted from several cases where patients taking Levitra reported sudden hearing loss, sometimes with dizziness and ringing in the ears.


- **FindLaw also reported:** 
Shortly after the FDA approved Levitra, the agency began to issue safety alerts about the drug. Specifically, the FDA ordered Bayer and other manufacturers of vardenafil, such as GlaxoSmithKline, to add black box warnings to their products' labels.


- **Nitrate Contraindication (Boxed Warning):** 
Vardenafil hydrochloride tablets can potentiate the hypotensive effects of nitrates, alpha-blockers, and antihypertensives
 — a contraindication that is prominently displayed in the prescribing information. 
Patients should be counseled that concomitant use of vardenafil with nitrates could cause blood pressure to suddenly drop to an unsafe level, resulting in dizziness, syncope, or even heart attack or stroke.


- **QT Prolongation Warning:** 
Patients with congenital QT syndrome or taking class IA or III antiarrhythmics should avoid using vardenafil hydrochloride tablets.


---

### 3. 🔵 Has It Been Discontinued for Safety Reasons?

**No — but it has been discontinued commercially.** 
Levitra (vardenafil) remains one of the most recognizable names among erectile dysfunction (ED) medications, yet the brand itself has been marked as officially discontinued in several major markets, including the United States. This discontinuation often leads to confusion, with some users assuming that the drug was removed for safety or efficacy concerns. In reality, the reason is far simpler: business strategy and market dynamics, not medical risk.



Importantly, the active ingredient (vardenafil) was not discontinued. Generic vardenafil remains fully available and FDA-, EMA-, and internationally approved. The safety profile of the drug has not changed, and clinical evidence supporting its effectiveness remains robust.

---

## Has Sildenafil Been Withdrawn, Given a Black Box Warning, or Discontinued for Safety Reasons?

### ✅ Short Answer: **No full market withdrawal**, but there have been **significant safety warnings**, a **pediatric use warning**, and a **petition for a black box warning** (which was not granted).

---

## 1. 🚫 No Global Market Withdrawal

Sildenafil has **not been withdrawn from any market for safety or effectiveness reasons**. 
The FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database contains decades of post-marketing safety data for sildenafil, and the drug's safety profile has been remarkably consistent with what was observed in registration trials.
 Furthermore, 
post-market surveillance data spanning over 25 years have not identified new safety signals beyond those in the original label.


The FDA's official list of drugs withdrawn for safety or efficacy reasons (21 CFR 216.24) does **not** include sildenafil. [See the eCFR list here](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-216/subpart-B/section-216.24).

---

## 2. ⚠️ FDA Pediatric Safety Warning (2012) — Revatio (Sildenafil for PAH in Children)

This is the most significant regulatory safety action taken against sildenafil.


The FDA revised the sildenafil drug label in August 2012, adding a warning stating that "use of sildenafil, particularly chronic use, is not recommended in children." This recommendation was based on an observation of increasing mortality with increasing sildenafil doses in a long-term clinical trial in pediatric patients with PAH.



According to the FDA, the purpose of the recommendation was to raise awareness of clinical trial results showing a higher risk of mortality in pediatric patients taking a high dose of sildenafil compared to those taking a low dose. However, the agency said the recommendation was not intended to suggest that sildenafil should **never** be used in children.


The FDA later clarified this warning. 
In a statement announcing the clarification, the FDA said: "The evidence behind our initial recommendation has not changed; we are simply clarifying the strength of the warning communicated in the drug label." The FDA further recognized "there may be situations in which the benefit-risk profile of sildenafil may be acceptable in individual children, for example, when other treatment options are limited and sildenafil can be used with close monitoring."


📌 Source: [FDA Drug Safety Communications – Sildenafil (Viagra and Revatio)](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/postmarket-drug-safety-information-patients-and-providers/sildenafil-marketed-viagra-and-revatio-information)
📌 Source: [American College of Cardiology – FDA Issues Clarification on Sildenafil Use in Children](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/articles/2014/04/14/11/18/fda-issues-clarification-on-sildenafil-use-in-children-with-pah)

## 3. ⚠️ Vision Loss Warning Added to Label (2005)


In July 2005, the FDA updated labeling for tadalafil (Cialis), vardenafil (Levitra), and sildenafil (Viagra) to reflect a small number of post-marketing reports of sudden vision loss, while acknowledging that "it is not possible to determine whether these oral medicines for erectile dysfunction were the cause of the loss of eyesight or whether the problem is related to other factors such as high blood pressure or diabetes."


Specifically, the condition of concern was **non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION)**. 
When used to treat erectile dysfunction, NAION — a cause of decreased vision including permanent loss of vision — has been reported post-marketing in temporal association with the use of PDE-5 inhibitors, including sildenafil. Most patients had underlying anatomic or vascular risk factors for developing NAION, including low cup to disc ratio ("crowded disc").


📌 Source: [DailyMed – Sildenafil Label (FDA)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=d887377e-90c5-44dc-8455-b23a6755b36f)

---

## 4. 📋 Black Box Warning — Petitioned But NOT Granted


Public Citizen petitioned the FDA to immediately add a black box warning regarding the risks of drug-induced blindness for PDE5 inhibitors prescribed for erectile dysfunction — Viagra (sildenafil), Cialis (tadalafil), and Levitra (vardenafil). The label for Revatio, a version of sildenafil for pulmonary arterial hypertension, was also included in the recommended changes.



The petition noted that the number of cases of ischemic optic neuropathy per million prescriptions was 18-fold higher for patients taking Viagra compared with patients taking Lipitor, another drug used by people with similar risk factors.


However, the FDA did **not** grant a formal black box warning for sildenafil in response to this petition. Instead, a standard warning about vision loss was added to the label (as noted above).

📌 Source: [Public Citizen – Petition to Require a Black Box Warning for ED Drugs](https://www.citizen.org/article/petition-to-require-a-black-box-warning-for-erectile-dysfunction-drugs-sildenafil-viagra-tadalafil-cialis-and-vardenafil-levitra/)
📌 Source: [PMC – Inadequate Warnings About ED Drug Blindness Risk](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1681722/)

---

## 5. 🇪🇺 EMA Withdrawal of "Sildenafil FGK" Application (2021) — Not a Safety Withdrawal


FGK Representative Service GmbH withdrew its application for a marketing authorisation of Sildenafil FGK for the treatment of adult men with erectile dysfunction. The company withdrew the application on 19 July 2021.
 Importantly, 
Sildenafil FGK was a "hybrid medicine," meaning it contained the same active substance as Viagra but was to be available as a thin sublingual strip (placed under the tongue), not the standard oral tablet.
 
The EMA's provisional opinion was that Sildenafil FGK could not have been authorised for the treatment of erectile dysfunction, as the data submitted did not support the sublingual use.
 This was a **withdrawal of a specific novel formulation's marketing application**, not a safety withdrawal of sildenafil itself.

📌 Source: [EMA – Sildenafil FGK Withdrawal](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/sildenafil-fgk)

---

The current sildenafil label carries several important (non-black-box) warnings, including:
- 
Contraindication with concomitant use of organic nitrates in any form, due to the greater risk of hypotension.

- 
Pulmonary hypertension secondary to sickle cell disease: Sildenafil may cause serious vaso-occlusive crises.

Here’s a target-focused answer using the disease biology of **idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH)** and the fact that **sildenafil shows IC50/Ki activity against PDE5A, implying inhibition of PDE5A**.

## 1) Disease mechanism

**Core pathophysiological defect in IPAH:**  
IPAH is fundamentally a disease of **pulmonary vascular remodeling plus sustained vasoconstriction**, which raises pulmonary vascular resistance. A central molecular abnormality is **reduced NO–sGC–cGMP signaling** in the pulmonary circulation, alongside endothelial dysfunction and abnormal smooth-muscle proliferation. In pulmonary artery smooth muscle, **PDE5A degrades cGMP**, so increased PDE5A activity/expression would further suppress this protective vasodilatory, anti-proliferative pathway. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8977136/?utm_source=openai))

**Is PDE5A deficient or overactive in IPAH?**  
The evidence supports **PDE5A being overactive/upregulated rather than deficient**. Human IPAH studies report **increased PDE5A expression** in relevant disease tissue/cells, including pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells from IPAH patients. One transcriptomic study states that **PDE5A is significantly increased in IPAH PASMCs**, and another study found **enhanced PDE5A expression** in PASMCs from IPAH compared with controls. A platelet-signaling study in IPAH also reported **increased expression of PDE5A**, consistent with impaired NO responsiveness. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348089/?utm_source=openai))

**Conclusion for Q1:**  
In IPAH, the disease-relevant PDE5A state is best described as **overactive/elevated function**, driven at least in part by **increased PDE5A expression causing excess cGMP breakdown** in the pulmonary vasculature. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348089/?utm_source=openai))

## 2) Target-specific direction

Given your constraint to focus **only on the drug’s direct action on PDE5A itself**:

- **Sildenafil has inhibitory activity against PDE5A** by inference from IC50/Ki assay activity.
- In IPAH, **PDE5A is increased/overactive**.
- Therefore, **direct inhibition of PDE5A would correct or compensate for the disease defect**, not worsen it. By inhibiting the overactive enzyme, sildenafil would oppose the abnormal excess degradation of cGMP attributable to PDE5A. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348089/?utm_source=openai))

So the target-specific direction is:

**PDE5A inhibitor on an overactive/upregulated PDE5A background = corrective/compensatory.** ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348089/?utm_source=openai))

## 3) Clinical use anchor

**Yes. Sildenafil is an approved treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension.**  
The FDA label for **REVATIO (sildenafil)** states it is indicated for **pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group I)** in adults. The same official labeling describes sildenafil’s mechanism as **inhibition of cGMP-specific PDE-5 in the smooth muscle of the pulmonary vasculature**, where PDE-5 is responsible for **degradation of cGMP**. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/021845s025lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))

This means the **confirmed clinical mechanism through PDE5A/PDE5** is:

- **PDE5 inhibition in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle**
- **reduced cGMP degradation**
- thereby restoring/augmenting the deficient NO–cGMP signaling axis in PAH. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/203109s016lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))

A closely related compound in the same class is also established clinically: **tadalafil**, another **PDE5 inhibitor**, is approved for PAH as well, reinforcing that **PDE5 inhibition is a validated therapeutic mechanism in this disease class.** ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/021845s025lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))

## Bottom line

1. **Disease defect:** IPAH features impaired pulmonary vascular NO–cGMP signaling, vascular remodeling, and vasoconstriction; **PDE5A is overactive/upregulated**, not deficient. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348089/?utm_source=openai))  
2. **Direction of sildenafil on PDE5A:** Because sildenafil inhibits PDE5A and PDE5A is elevated in IPAH, its direct action on PDE5A would **correct/compensate for** the defect. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348089/?utm_source=openai))  
3. **Clinical anchor:** Yes—**sildenafil is an approved PAH therapy**, and its confirmed mechanism is **PDE5 inhibition in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle, reducing cGMP breakdown**. ## Alprostadil: Withdrawals, Black Box Warnings, and Discontinuations

### 1. ✅ BLACK BOX WARNING (IV/Neonatal Use — Apnea)

Alprostadil **does carry a Black Box Warning** — but only for the **intravenous (IV) formulation** used in neonates (brand: Prostin VR Pediatric), not for the adult erectile dysfunction (ED) formulations.


Apnea is experienced by about 10 to 12% of neonates with congenital heart defects treated with alprostadil injection. Apnea is most often seen in neonates weighing less than 2 kg at birth and usually appears during the first hour of drug infusion. Therefore, respiratory status should be monitored throughout treatment, and alprostadil injection should be used where ventilatory assistance is immediately available.


This warning is prominently placed in a **WARNING box** on the official FDA-approved prescribing label. 
Alprostadil injection, USP should be administered only by trained personnel in facilities that provide pediatric intensive care.


Additionally, 
the administration of alprostadil injection to neonates may result in gastric outlet obstruction secondary to antral hyperplasia. This effect appears to be related to duration of therapy and cumulative dose of the drug. Neonates receiving alprostadil injection at recommended doses for more than 120 hours should be closely monitored for evidence of antral hyperplasia and gastric outlet obstruction.

One major brand of alprostadil — **MUSE® (Medicated Urethral System for Erection)** — has been discontinued, though **not for safety reasons**.


Muse® was a urethral suppository medication containing the active ingredient alprostadil, a prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) analog. It was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat erectile dysfunction (ED) but was discontinued in June 2024 and is no longer available in the U.S.



Viatris discontinued Muse in June 2024. Viatris has discontinued all presentations of Muse urethral suppositories.

### 3. ✅ LIMITED RECALL (Edex® — One Lot Only, Manufacturing Defect) — 2017

One specific lot of **Edex® (alprostadil for injection)** was voluntarily recalled, but due to a **manufacturing defect — not a safety-related drug action**.


Endo Pharmaceuticals Inc. announced a voluntary recall of one lot of Edex® (alprostadil for injection) 10 mcg to the consumer level. This product recall was due to the detection by Endo of a defect in the crimp caps used in the manufacture of the subject product lot.
 
This recall has been completed and the FDA has terminated this recall.

For the adult-use ED formulations (Caverject, Edex), the FDA label contains several important safety warnings:

- **Priapism:** 
Alprostadil may cause an unwanted erection that may be persistent, painful, and that may occur without sexual arousal. Permanent damage to the penis may occur if priapism is not treated quickly.

- **Penile fibrosis:** 
Physical examination of the penis should be performed periodically to detect signs of penile fibrosis. Treatment with CAVERJECT IMPULSE should be discontinued in patients who develop penile angulation or cavernosal fibrosis.

1. **Disease mechanism / PTGIR direction**

Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) is driven by **pulmonary arteriolar vasoconstriction plus pathologic vascular remodeling**—especially proliferation/resistance to apoptosis of pulmonary artery smooth-muscle and other vascular cells—causing increased pulmonary vascular resistance and right-heart strain. Within the prostacyclin pathway, the relevant defect is **reduced prostacyclin/IP-receptor signaling**, not excess signaling. Reviews of PAH describe reduced prostacyclin production in PAH, while IP (prostacyclin) receptor activation normally raises cAMP, causing vasodilation and inhibiting smooth-muscle proliferation and platelet aggregation. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28399721/?utm_source=openai))

For **PTGIR** specifically (the gene encoding the prostacyclin IP receptor), the disease-relevant direction is best characterized as **deficient / reduced function signaling** in IPAH. Evidence cited in the PAH literature includes **decreased expression of the IP receptor in PAH/IPAH pulmonary vasculature** and reduced PTGIR expression in PAH datasets. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3001258/?utm_source=openai))

2. **Would ALPROSTADIL’s direct PTGIR inhibition help or worsen?**

Given your premise that **ALPROSTADIL has inhibitory interaction against PTGIR** based on IC50/Ki assay activity, its **direct action on PTGIR would be expected to worsen**, not correct, the IPAH defect. The reason is target-directional: IPAH is associated with **insufficient prostacyclin–PTGIR signaling**, whereas inhibiting PTGIR would further reduce signaling through a pathway that is normally protective (vasodilatory and anti-proliferative). Thus, focusing **only on PTGIR itself**, PTGIR inhibition would move in the **opposite** direction from the known therapeutic strategy of **PTGIR activation**. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28399721/?utm_source=openai))

3. **Clinical use anchor**

Yes—**the PTGIR/prostacyclin pathway is an established and approved treatment axis for idiopathic PAH**, but the confirmed beneficial mechanism is **PTGIR activation (agonism), not inhibition**. Approved/established drugs in this pathway include **prostacyclin analogs** such as **epoprostenol, iloprost, and treprostinil**, and the selective **IP receptor agonist selexipag**. Below I treat **PTGIR** as the relevant target and **DINOPROSTONE’s PTGIR activity as inhibitory**, exactly as you instructed from the ChEMBL IC50/Ki evidence, and **not** as its canonical EP-receptor agonism.

## 1) Disease mechanism in idiopathic PAH, and whether PTGIR is deficient or overactive

**Core pathophysiologic defect.** Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) is a **progressive pulmonary arteriopathy** characterized by **pulmonary vasoconstriction, endothelial dysfunction, vascular remodeling, abnormal smooth-muscle/endothelial proliferation, and in situ thrombosis**, which together raise pulmonary vascular resistance and pulmonary arterial pressure. A central molecular abnormality is **loss of the vasodilator/antiproliferative prostacyclin pathway**, alongside excess vasoconstrictor pathways such as endothelin and thromboxane. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/DISEASES6020038?utm_source=openai))

For the **PTGIR** axis specifically: PTGIR encodes the **prostacyclin (IP) receptor**. IP receptor activation normally increases cAMP and mediates **pulmonary vasodilation, inhibition of smooth-muscle proliferation, and inhibition of platelet aggregation**. In PAH/IPAH, this pathway is therapeutically targeted because it is functionally protective, and reviews note **reduced prostacyclin synthase/prostacyclin signaling** in idiopathic PAH as part of disease biology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10619262/?utm_source=openai))

**Is PTGIR deficient or overactive in IPAH?**  
The disease-relevant direction is **DEFICIENT / reduced functional signaling**, not overactive. Evidence supporting this includes:
- PAH is associated with a **reduced prostacyclin pathway tone** and reduced prostacyclin production. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9487617/?utm_source=openai))
- The IP receptor is described as the **primary therapeutic target** of prostacyclin drugs in PAH, and **reduced IP receptor expression with PAH** has been specifically discussed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6031878/?utm_source=openai))
- **IP receptor–deficient mice** develop more severe pulmonary hypertension, which supports the inference that **loss of PTGIR function worsens** the pulmonary hypertensive phenotype. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6031878/?utm_source=openai))

So, at the target-mechanism level most relevant to IPAH therapy, **PTGIR activity is insufficient/protective-loss rather than pathologically excessive**. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6031878/?utm_source=openai))

## 2) Would PTGIR inhibition by dinoprostone correct or worsen that defect?

Given your constraint that **DINOPROSTONE acts as an inhibitor on PTGIR** based on ChEMBL IC50/Ki binding data, its **direct action on PTGIR would be expected to WORSEN**, not correct, the IPAH defect. The reason is straightforward:

- PTGIR/IP signaling is **protective** in pulmonary arterial hypertension: activation promotes **vasodilation** and **antiproliferative** effects in the pulmonary vasculature. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10619262/?utm_source=openai))
- IPAH already involves **reduced prostacyclin-pathway signaling**. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9487617/?utm_source=openai))
- Therefore, **inhibiting PTGIR directly** would further suppress a pathway that the disease is lacking, so it would be expected to **aggravate/oppose compensation for the disease mechanism** rather than restore it. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6031878/?utm_source=openai))

So the target-specific answer is: **direct PTGIR inhibition by dinoprostone would worsen the disease-relevant PTGIR defect**. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6031878/?utm_source=openai))

## 3) Clinical use anchor: is dinoprostone or a close class relative used for IPAH/PTGIR dysfunction, and what is the confirmed PTGIR mechanism?

**Dinoprostone itself:** I did **not** find evidence that **dinoprostone (PGE2)** is an approved or established treatment for IPAH. Its approved clinical use is obstetric/gynecologic (for example, cervical ripening/labor induction), not pulmonary arterial hypertension. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK545279/?utm_source=openai))

**Closely related class members:** **Yes** — drugs in the **prostacyclin pathway class** are established therapies for PAH/IPAH, but their confirmed beneficial mechanism is the **opposite direction at PTGIR**: they are **PTGIR/IP receptor agonists**, not inhibitors.
- **Selexipag** is FDA-labeled as a **prostacyclin receptor agonist** indicated for **pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1)**. ([dailymed.nlm.nih.gov](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=ff660787-880f-4f2b-baac-fd2dbfcd79c2&utm_source=openai))
- Reviews also identify **epoprostenol, iloprost, and treprostinil** as approved prostacyclin-pathway therapies for PAH. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7389678/?utm_source=openai))
- The mechanistic rationale through PTGIR is confirmed as **IP receptor activation**, producing **increased cAMP, pulmonary vasodilation, and inhibition of vascular smooth-muscle proliferation/platelet aggregation**. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28399721/?utm_source=openai))

**For disease caused by PTGIR dysfunction:** I did not find a standard approved therapy specifically labeled as “for PTGIR deficiency” as a named monogenic disease. However, the available evidence supports that **reduced PTGIR signaling is deleterious**, and the clinically validated way to address this axis in PAH is **agonism of PTGIR**, not inhibition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7983006/?utm_source=openai))

## Bottom line

1. **IPAH core defect:** progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling/vasoconstriction with a **deficient prostacyclin–PTGIR protective pathway**. **PTGIR is functionally deficient/reduced, not overactive.** ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/DISEASES6020038?utm_source=openai))  
2. **Dinoprostone on PTGIR (as inhibitor):** would **WORSEN** the PTGIR-related disease defect, because PTGIR signaling is beneficial and already insufficient in IPAH. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10619262/?utm_source=openai))  
3. **Clinical anchor:** **dinoprostone itself is not an established IPAH treatment**; but **closely related prostacyclin-pathway drugs** are used in PAH, and their confirmed mechanism is **PTGIR agonism** (e.g., selexipag; also prostacyclin analogs), which is the opposite of PTGIR inhibition. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK545279/?utm_source=openai))
